SPI-01.title: Restore confidence in Main
SPI-01.action: Make the exact version on Main pass the repository's required build or validation and confirm that it is ready to release.
SPI-01.why_it_matters: Main is the approved source line for future releases. If its readiness is not proven, the organization cannot safely rely on the repository.
SPI-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A successful, current build or validation record tied to the exact assessed version on Main, with every required check complete.

SPI-02.title: Identify the source of every live or published output
SPI-02.action: Record the exact, unchangeable source version behind every currently running, published, distributed, or supported output and show that it came through Main.
SPI-02.why_it_matters: Leaders need to know what is in use and where it came from so incidents, audits, and corrections can be handled decisively.
SPI-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A complete list of current outputs with an unchangeable release identity and a verified link back to Main for each one.

SPI-03.title: Give every release a permanent identity
SPI-03.action: Assign every supported release a unique identity that cannot be overwritten and retain a verifiable record of how it was produced.
SPI-03.why_it_matters: A permanent release identity prevents a named version from changing silently and makes investigations and recovery dependable.
SPI-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Every sampled release has a permanent source identity, output identity, and production record that agree.

SPI-04.title: Define how Main corresponds to what is in use
SPI-04.action: Choose and document, for each product or output, the approved relationship between Main and the version currently in use, then surface any departure from it.
SPI-04.why_it_matters: A clear operating rule distinguishes intentional release timing from uncontrolled drift.
SPI-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A named correspondence rule for every in-scope output, with current records showing either conformance or an owned correction plan.

BTC-01.title: Make the build or validation repeatable
BTC-01.action: Provide one documented, non-interactive way to build or validate the repository from a clean copy using declared inputs.
BTC-01.why_it_matters: The organization should not depend on one person's computer or undocumented knowledge to recreate or verify its work.
BTC-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A version-controlled command or process and a recent successful run from a clean copy.

BTC-02.title: Check every accepted change automatically
BTC-02.action: Ensure every proposed and accepted change triggers the required automated validation for the exact version that will be placed on Main.
BTC-02.why_it_matters: Consistent automatic checks catch avoidable problems and show that accepted work was actually verified.
BTC-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Every change in the assessment window is linked to a completed validation result for the accepted version.

BTC-03.title: Match validation to the risk of each change
BTC-03.action: Define which checks each kind of change requires and prevent acceptance until all applicable checks are complete.
BTC-03.why_it_matters: Important changes need stronger proof, while low-risk changes should still receive the checks that matter to them.
BTC-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current change-to-check matrix and complete results for every sampled change category.

BTC-04.title: Shorten the wait for change feedback
BTC-04.action: Set an approved time target for required validation and address the steps that regularly exceed it.
BTC-04.why_it_matters: Timely feedback supports smaller, safer changes and reduces pressure to bypass safeguards.
BTC-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A documented time target and measured results showing that at least 95 percent of required feedback completes within it.

BTC-05.title: Make validation results dependable
BTC-05.action: Identify checks that change result without a meaningful source change, correct their causes, and time-limit any temporary quarantine.
BTC-05.why_it_matters: Unreliable checks train people to ignore failures and can hide real defects.
BTC-05.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Measured repeatability within the standard threshold and an owned, dated record for any temporarily isolated check.

CGD-01.title: Control and record every change to Main
CGD-01.action: Require every accepted change to Main to retain who made it, who authorized it, what validation passed, and whether an emergency path was used.
CGD-01.why_it_matters: A complete decision trail provides accountability and lets the organization explain exactly how accepted work entered Main.
CGD-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A complete, current audit chain for every sampled change, including any emergency or privileged change.

CGD-02.title: Protect Main and every production-critical source line
CGD-02.action: Prevent unauthorized changes, deletion, and history rewriting on Main and every source line or release label that can affect production.
CGD-02.why_it_matters: These protections prevent one unapproved action from changing or erasing the organization's accepted and released work.
CGD-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A complete inventory of production-critical source lines and release labels, effective protection settings, limited bypass access, and a successful protection test.

CGD-03.title: Require an independent review where risk warrants it
CGD-03.action: Have an authorized person other than the author approve the final version of each in-scope change before acceptance.
CGD-03.why_it_matters: Independent review reduces accidental and harmful changes and spreads understanding beyond the author.
CGD-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Every sampled in-scope change shows the required independent approval for its final accepted version.

CGD-04.title: Prevent acceptance when required checks are incomplete
CGD-04.action: Configure the repository so a change cannot be accepted while a required check is missing, failed, or attached to an earlier version.
CGD-04.why_it_matters: A written rule only protects the organization when the acceptance process consistently enforces it.
CGD-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Protection settings and sampled changes show that only the final, fully validated version can be accepted.

CGD-05.title: Bring actual work practices back in line with the declared method
CGD-05.action: Compare observed change, branch, release, and urgent-fix practices with the declared working method and correct or formally update each material difference.
CGD-05.why_it_matters: A method that differs from actual behavior creates hidden risk and makes controls unreliable.
CGD-05.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Current practice and the declared method agree, with any approved hybrid practice explicitly documented and evidenced.

CGD-06.title: Limit and account for emergency or privileged changes
CGD-06.action: Restrict emergency and privileged access, record why each use was necessary, review it promptly, and remove temporary access on time.
CGD-06.why_it_matters: Emergency paths may be necessary, but untracked or standing privilege can bypass the safeguards leaders rely on.
CGD-06.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current access list and a complete, timely record for every privileged or emergency change in the assessment window.

SSC-01.title: Prevent exposed passwords, keys, and tokens
SSC-01.action: Block sensitive credentials from entering the repository, review existing history, and use a tested response process when exposure occurs.
SSC-01.why_it_matters: An exposed credential can give an unauthorized person access to systems or data even after the source change is removed.
SSC-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Active prevention, a current history review, and evidence that any detected credential was disabled, replaced, and investigated on time.

SSC-02.title: Maintain a complete inventory of outside components
SSC-02.action: Produce and retain a current inventory of the outside software and services included in each released product.
SSC-02.why_it_matters: The organization cannot respond confidently to a supplier problem if it does not know which products include the affected component.
SSC-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Every sampled release has a complete, machine-readable component inventory tied to that exact release.

SSC-03.title: Resolve high-risk component problems on time
SSC-03.action: Assign, prioritize, and correct known component and security problems within the approved time limits, or record a time-limited risk decision.
SSC-03.why_it_matters: Known high-risk weaknesses become more likely to cause harm when ownership or deadlines are unclear.
SSC-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current problem register with owner, due date, disposition, and no overdue item outside an approved, unexpired risk decision.

SSC-04.title: Protect the release automation itself
SSC-04.action: Limit automation permissions, fix outside automation components to reviewed versions, protect sensitive values, and approve changes to release workflows.
SSC-04.why_it_matters: Compromised release automation can alter products even when the source itself was reviewed correctly.
SSC-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A reviewed automation configuration with minimum permissions, protected sensitive values, fixed component versions, and controlled workflow changes.

OWM-01.title: Name an accountable owner and backup
OWM-01.action: Assign a current business or product owner, a technical owner, and a backup route for the repository, then confirm that each accepts the role.
OWM-01.why_it_matters: Improvement work and urgent decisions stall when no one is clearly accountable.
OWM-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Current ownership records, acknowledged responsibilities, and a tested escalation route.

OWM-02.title: Remove single-person dependency from critical work
OWM-02.action: Identify work that only one person can safely perform and transfer enough knowledge and access to at least one qualified backup.
OWM-02.why_it_matters: A single-person dependency can stop releases, recovery, or support when that person is unavailable.
OWM-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Named primary and backup owners for every critical area, with a recent successful handoff, review, or recovery exercise.

OWM-03.title: Keep the toolchain and known obligations current
OWM-03.action: List supported tools and versions, assign owners to outdated or unsupported items, and track each material obligation to a dated decision.
OWM-03.why_it_matters: Unsupported tools and unowned maintenance needs make future changes and recovery less predictable.
OWM-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current toolchain record and an owned register of material upgrades, debt, and end-of-support dates.

OWM-04.title: Make source changes reviewable
OWM-04.action: Keep the human-maintained source clear, separate generated output, and document how generated material can be reproduced and reviewed.
OWM-04.why_it_matters: Reviewers cannot judge a change reliably when generated or unreadable material hides what people actually changed.
OWM-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A documented source/output boundary, reproducible generation process, and reviewable sampled changes.

DCR-01.title: Provide a clear starting guide
DCR-01.action: Give a new reader a current explanation of the repository's purpose, owner, status, Main line, outputs, and basic validation steps.
DCR-01.why_it_matters: Clear orientation reduces delays, incorrect assumptions, and dependency on informal knowledge.
DCR-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current starting document that a new contributor can follow successfully.

DCR-02.title: Document how work is proposed, checked, and released
DCR-02.action: Explain the actual path for proposing, reviewing, validating, accepting, and releasing changes, including urgent changes.
DCR-02.why_it_matters: People are more likely to follow controls when the expected path is clear and matches reality.
DCR-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current contributor guide that matches observed practice and covers the normal and urgent paths.

DCR-03.title: Publish support and security reporting routes
DCR-03.action: State where users and contributors should report support needs and sensitive security concerns, who responds, and the expected response time.
DCR-03.why_it_matters: Clear reporting routes help the right people receive and contain problems before they spread.
DCR-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Visible, tested support and private security-reporting routes with named owners and response expectations.

DCR-04.title: Clarify rights, versions, and release changes
DCR-04.action: Document use rights, the versioning approach, supported versions, and material changes for every published or distributed output.
DCR-04.why_it_matters: Consumers need to know what they may use, what changed, and which versions the organization still supports.
DCR-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Current rights, version, support, and release-change records for each in-scope output.

RRO-01.title: Create one complete release record
RRO-01.action: For every release, retain the approval, accepted source version, validation result, output identity, destination, and release result in one connected record.
RRO-01.why_it_matters: A complete release record lets the organization prove what changed and act quickly when a correction is needed.
RRO-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Every sampled release has a complete and internally consistent evidence chain.

RRO-02.title: Practice the recovery or withdrawal path
RRO-02.action: Define the safe way to reverse, correct, withdraw, or supersede each output and exercise that path at the required interval.
RRO-02.why_it_matters: A recovery plan that has not been practiced may fail when customers or operations are already under pressure.
RRO-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current recovery path for each output and a successful, recent exercise with actions from any lessons learned.

RRO-03.title: Control the path into production
RRO-03.action: Allow only approved release identities and authorized people or automation to change production, with the result recorded.
RRO-03.why_it_matters: A controlled production path prevents unreviewed or unidentified work from reaching users.
RRO-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: Current access and promotion rules plus sampled records showing only approved releases reached production.

RRO-04.title: Confirm operational readiness before release
RRO-04.action: Define and complete the required monitoring, support, response, and recovery readiness checks before each material release.
RRO-04.why_it_matters: A technically successful release can still disrupt the business when support and recovery are not ready.
RRO-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A risk-based readiness checklist and completed evidence for every sampled material release.

RLP-01.title: Complete the repository's portfolio record
RLP-01.action: Record the repository's purpose, type, lifecycle, risk, authority, owner, Main line, outputs, and review date in the portfolio inventory.
RLP-01.why_it_matters: Leaders cannot govern cost, risk, or retirement decisions without a reliable inventory.
RLP-01.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A complete, current portfolio record that agrees with repository and production evidence.

RLP-02.title: Remove or govern stale source lines and release labels
RLP-02.action: Review old branches and release labels, delete those with no continuing purpose, and assign an owner and expiry to every approved exception.
RLP-02.why_it_matters: Unmanaged old lines create confusion, hide unsupported work, and can preserve unsafe access paths.
RLP-02.expected_evidence_or_outcome: A current inventory with disposition, owner, and expiry for every stale item.

RLP-03.title: Make retirement safe and explicit
RLP-03.action: When an output or repository is deprecated, archived, or retired, notify consumers, preserve required records, remove active access, and name any successor.
RLP-03.why_it_matters: An incomplete retirement leaves consumers on unsupported work and can leave forgotten access or obligations behind.
RLP-03.expected_evidence_or_outcome: An approved retirement record showing consumer notice, successor or final-state guidance, preserved evidence, and removed active paths.

RLP-04.title: Identify the one authoritative repository
RLP-04.action: Name the authoritative repository for each product and clearly mark every mirror, fork, or duplicate so people do not release from the wrong source.
RLP-04.why_it_matters: Competing copies create uncertainty about ownership, accepted changes, and the source of releases.
RLP-04.expected_evidence_or_outcome: One confirmed authoritative repository per product, with all other copies labeled and governed for their intended purpose.
